AND TONIGHT WE BEGIN WITH A SHOT OF THE GLORIOUS FULL MOON TONIGHT, AS ARTEMIS TWO HEADS IN HER DIRECTION. GOOD EVENING. THANK YOU FOR JOINING US. I’M SUMMER KNOWLES, I’M JESSE PAGAN. QUITE THE DAY IN CENTRAL FLORIDA. AS ARTEMIS TWO LAUNCHED TO THE MOON IN WESH, WHO HAS BEEN WITH IT EVERY STEP OF THE WAY. WE BEGIN OUR TEAM COVERAGE TONIGHT OF ARTEMIS LAUNCH WITH WESH TWO’S MEGAN MORIARTY MEAGHAN BACK LIVE AT HER POST AT KENNEDY SPACE CENTER A COUPLE HOURS NOW. AFTER THAT LAUNCH, MEGAN. I’M GOING TO CHANGE MY HOME ADDRESS TO KENNEDY SPACE CENTER AT THIS POINT, BUT I’M REALLY EXCITED AND FEEL VERY LUCKY THAT WE GOT TO SEE THAT LAUNCH RIGHT HERE FROM THE PRESS SITE. NOW, THERE WERE SOME CONCERNS GOING INTO THIS LAUNCH. FIRST AND FOREMOST, THE WEATHER AND THEN HYDROGEN LEAKS IS ALWAYS A TOP CONCERN. BUT WE LEARNED FROM THAT NEWS CONFERENCE THAT HYDROGEN LEAKS WERE AT LESS THAN 1%, WHICH IS INCREDIBLE. AND THEN THE WEATHER ACTUALLY GOT BETTER THROUGHOUT THE DAY. BUT WHILE THIS WAS A NEAR FLAWLESS LAUNCH, THERE WERE A FEW BUMPS IN THE ROAD. THREE TWO, ONE BOOSTER IGNITION AND LIFTOFF. THE CREW OF ARTEMIS TWO, NOW BOUND FOR THE MOON. HUMANITY’S NEXT GREAT VOYAGE BEGINS. GOOD LUCK. GODSPEED, ARM TWO. LET’S GO. ROGER. ROLL PITCH! AFTER A BRIEF 54 YEAR INTERMISSION, NASA IS BACK IN THE BUSINESS OF SENDING ASTRONAUTS TO THE MOON, A MISSION YEARS IN THE MAKING IS NOW ON ITS WAY. A TRULY EXCEPTIONAL CREW UP THERE THAT HAVE BEEN TRAINING FOR YEARS ON THIS, THAT GIVES YOU THE CONFIDENCE TO UNDERTAKE THIS MISSION, ESPECIALLY KNOWING THE IMPLICATIONS THAT IT IS PART OF A MUCH BIGGER PROGRAM. AND HERE THEY ARE. NASA’S ARTEMIS TWO CREW COMMANDER, REID WISEMAN, PILOT VICTOR GLOVER AND MISSION SPECIALIST CHRISTINA COOK AND JEREMY HANSEN ARE HEADING TO THE MOON. THE CREW SUITED UP WEDNESDAY AFTERNOON, COMPLETING SUCCESSFUL HEALTH CHECKS. THEN, AS TRADITION HAS IT, THE ARTEMIS TWO TEAM PLAYED A CARD GAME. IT’S MEANT TO GET RID OF ANY BAD LUCK AHEAD OF THE LAUNCH. AFTER WAVING GOODBYE TO THEIR FAMILY AND FRIENDS, THEY DROVE OUT TO LAUNCH PAD 39. B, WENT UP THE ELEVATOR TO THE ORION CAPSULE AND WAITED FOR LIFTOFF. BUT THE LAUNCH WASN’T WITHOUT A FEW ISSUES. NOW, ABOUT 51 MINUTES INTO THE FLIGHT, DURING A PLANNED HANDOVER BETWEEN SATELLITES, THE ORION SPACECRAFT UNDERWENT A COMMUNICATIONS ISSUE, COMES WITH THE CREW HAVE BEEN RESTORED. ULTIMATELY, CREWS WERE ABLE TO WORK THROUGH IT. WE’VE CERTAINLY BEEN HERE BEFORE. WE KNOW THE CHALLENGES AHEAD. AND WHEN ALL GOES WELL. ARTEMIS TWO WILL BE MOON BOUND. AND SO TOMORROW NIGHT AT 630, THE NEXT STEP IS THE SPACECRAFT WILL CONDUCT WHAT’S CALLED A TRANSLUNAR INJECTION BURN. SO WHAT THAT WILL DO IS IT WILL HELP THE SPACECRAFT, WHICH WILL BE IN LOW EARTH ORBIT. IT WILL HELP MOVE IT FROM AN EARTH CENTRIC ORBIT TO A HIGHLY ECCENTRIC ORBIT TOWARDS THE MOON. AND AGAIN, THE MOON IS THE MISSION HERE, BUT WE’RE GOING TO HANG OUT IN LOW EARTH ORBIT FOR A LITTLE BIT JUST TO MAKE SURE EVERYTHING IS GOOD BEFORE TRANSCENDING IN THAT DIRECTION. THIS IS A TEN DAY MISSION WITH A LOT MOR WATCH: Artemis II launches from Florida's Space Coast Updated: 11:05 PM EDT Apr 1, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Artemis II has successfully launched from Florida's Space Coast.Watch it in the player below. long-term Moon exploration campaign.The program's main goals include returning humans to the moon, building a sustained lunar presence, maturing technology and operations needed for human missions to Mars, and doing this all with international and commercial partners.The missions are each designated to different milestones, strategies and individual goals.Artemis IThis mission is complete.It was an uncrewed integrated flight test of the Space Launch System, which is a heavy-lift rocket that launches crews and large cargo toward the moon, and Orion, which is a crew spacecraft that carries astronauts to lunar orbit and returns them to Earth.SLS and Orion went around the moon and came back to Earth.The purpose of this mission was to validate deep-space performance and reentry before flying with a crew.>> Relive the launch of Artemis I here.Artemis IIThis mission is planned.Artemis II will be the first crewed mission to the moon, with the plan to fly around itThe purpose of the crewed flight is to prove life support, operations and high-speed returns with astronauts.Artemis III (This mission has changes as of Feb. 27)This mission is planned.Artemis III will be the first crewed lunar landing of the program, targeting the lunar South Pole region.The 10-day mission will include field geology, sample collection/return and deployed experiments.Four astronauts will launch in Orion, two will land on the moon for surface work, and then they will return to Orion for the journey back to Earth.Artemis IV and beyondThe future missions will aim to expand on capabilities toward sustained operations on the moon, such as more surface time, more cargo and infrastructure delivery, increased use of Gateway as a staging node, and progression toward an "Artemis Base Camp" style sustainable presence.Why the lunar South Pole?It has scientifically valuable terrain and ancient geology.It contains regions with water ice and other volatiles in permanently shadowed areas, which is key for science and potential resources.Its challenging conditions will help prove the systems needed for Mars-class missions.Crowd reactionsMore information Artemis II has successfully launched from Florida's Space Coast.Watch it in the player below.
